key_insight: Glioblastoma necrosis may be an active, mutation-driven process in which tumor-associated neutrophil extracellular traps and HMGB2 sustain a tumor-cell necroptosis loop.
clinical_relevance: MRI necrotic volume and HMGB2 expression may help identify high-risk glioblastoma, while the inflammatory cascade offers candidate therapeutic targets.
method: Integrated clinical MRI radiomics with public genomic datasets.
Mapped tumor niches using single-cell spatial transcriptomics and protein immunofluorescence.
Investigated inflammatory mechanisms in a TP53/PTEN/NF1 co-mutant mouse model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports public genomic datasets totaling n=3,639, an independent association between MRI necrotic volume and poor survival, and multi-cohort validation of an HMGB2-high risk signature.
watch_item: Therapeutic findings remain preclinical; the abstract does not establish patient benefit or describe an AI drug-discovery method.
paper_title: Tumor Associated Neutrophils Extend NETs To Spatially Drive Necroptosis In Glioblastoma
